questions.question: What is the angle (in degrees) between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 1:50 PM?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

Hour hand covers 3600 in 12 hours

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered in 60 minutes = 300

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 30/60 = 1/2°

__Calculation:__

Minute hand covers 360 in 60 minutes

60 minutes = 3600

1 minute = 360/60 ⇒ 1 minute = 60

Here, the given time is **1:50 PM**

Minutes = 50

Angle covered by the **minute hand** = 50 × 6 = 3000

Angle covered by the **hour hand** = 1 × 30 + 50 × ½ = 30 + 25 = 55°

Angle between the **hour and minute hands** = 300 − 55 = 2450

Hence, the angle between the hour and minute hands is **245°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M|over2

Here, **H = 1** and **M = 50**.

So, Angle = |60 times 1 - 11 times 50|over2

Angle = |60 - 550|over2 = 490/2 = 245°

Hence, the correct answer is **245°**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 1 AM and 2 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock be opposite to each other?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The hands of a clock are opposite to each other when the angle between them is 1800

**Hour hand** covers 3600 in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 0.50

**Minute hand** covers 3600 in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the **minute hand** in 1 minute = 360/60 = 60

__Calculation:__

At **1 AM**, the position of the hands are:

**Hour hand** is at 1, which corresponds to 1 × 300 = 300 (from the 12 mark).

**Minute hand** is at 12, which corresponds to 00.

Let the hands be opposite after **m minutes** past 1 AM.

Position of **hour hand** = 30 + 0.5m

Position of **minute hand** = 6m

For the hands to be **opposite**, the difference between their angular positions must be 1800:

6m − (30 + 0.5m) = 180

5.5m − 30 = 180

5.5m = 210

m = 210 / 5.5 = 420 / 11

m = 38.1818... minutes

Therefore, the time is approximately **1:38 AM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle θ between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by:

θ = |30H − (11/2)M|

Here, H = 1 (since the time is between 1 and 2 AM) and θ = 1800 (opposite).

180 = |30(1) − (11/2)M|

Since the minute hand must cross the hour hand to be opposite, we take the positive result for (11/2)M − 30:

180 = (11/2)M − 30

210 = (11/2)M

M = 420 / 11

M ≈ 38.18

The approximate time is **1:38 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is **1:38**.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of two persons is 7: 8. The sum of their ages is 75. 10 years ago from now, what was the ratio of the ages of the two persons?

Sum of present ages = **75 years**

Let the present ages be **7x** and **8x**.

15x = 75

x = 5

First person's age = 35 − 10 = **25 years**

Second person's age = 40 − 10 = **30 years**

**Required ratio:**

25 : 30 = 5 : 6

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question: The emergence of Buddhism and Jainism in the 6th century BCE can be linked to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Criticism of Vedic rituals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **6th century BCE** in ancient India, often called the era of **Second Urbanization**, witnessed a significant socio-religious revolution known as the **Sramana movement**.
 
• The primary cause for the rise of **Buddhism** and **Jainism** was the deep-seated resentment against the **Brahmanical orthodoxy** and the increasingly complex **Vedic rituals**.
 
• The **Later Vedic period** saw the introduction of elaborate **sacrifices (Yajnas)** and **animal slaughter**, which were not only expensive for the common man but also hampered the burgeoning **agrarian economy** that required cattle for plowing.
 
• The **Varna system** had become rigid and hereditary, creating a social hierarchy that granted **Brahmins** supreme status, which was challenged by the **Kshatriyas** and the rising **Vaishya** (merchant) class.
 
• **Gautama Buddha** and **Lord Mahavira** rejected the **infallibility of the Vedas** and the necessity of priestly intervention, advocating for **ethical conduct**, **meditation**, and the principle of **Ahimsa (non-violence)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Transformation**:

 
 
• Contrary to the **decline of agriculture**, this period actually saw a massive expansion in farming due to the widespread use of **iron tools** and **plowshares** in the fertile **Middle Gangetic Valley**.
 
• The **Vaishyas**, who accumulated wealth through **trade and commerce**, supported **Buddhism** and **Jainism** because these religions provided them a higher social status compared to the **Vedic fold**.
 
 
 
• **Political and Cultural Factors**:
 
 
• The **rise of monarchies** and **Mahajanapadas** like **Magadha** provided the political stability necessary for these new ideologies to spread, as many rulers sought to curb the influence of the **priestly class**.
 
• The **Persian influence**, primarily through the **Achaemenid Empire**, was largely restricted to the **North-Western frontiers** and did not trigger the religious reformation occurring in the heartland of India.
 
• Both **Buddhism** and **Jainism** adopted local dialects like **Pali** and **Prakrit**, making their teachings accessible to the masses, unlike **Sanskrit** which was the exclusive domain of the elite.

questions.question: Which factor best explains the low sex ratio observed in northwestern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Female infanticide and socio-cultural bias**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sex ratio** in northwestern India, comprising states like **Haryana**, **Punjab**, and **Rajasthan**, has historically remained lower than the national average due to deep-seated **patriarchal** norms and a strong **son preference**.
 
• **Socio-cultural bias** stems from the perception of sons as economic assets and lineage carriers, while daughters are often viewed as economic liabilities, largely due to the prevalence of the **dowry system** and traditional inheritance customs.
 
• **Female infanticide**, the intentional killing of female infants, and **female foeticide**, the practice of sex-selective abortion, are the primary drivers behind the skewed **child sex ratio** in these regions.
 
• The misuse of medical technologies, such as **ultrasound** and **amniocentesis**, during the late **20th century** allowed for widespread illegal **sex determination**, leading to a sharp decline in female births.
 
• According to the **2011 Census**, the child sex ratio (0−6 years) in **Haryana** was recorded at a low of **834**, and **Punjab** at **846**, significantly below the national average of **919**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male-dominated migration**:

 
 
• While migration to urban industrial hubs like **Ludhiana** or **Gurugram** can affect the adult sex ratio in specific pockets, it does not account for the biological deficit of females at birth seen across the northwestern belt.
 
 
 
• **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act**:
 
 
• Enacted in **1994**, this federal law was designed to prevent **female foeticide** by banning the use of technology for sex selection and regulating prenatal diagnostic centers.
 
 
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)**:
 
 
• Launched in **January 2015**, this flagship government scheme specifically targets districts with a low **child sex ratio** to eliminate gender-biased sex selection and ensure the survival and protection of the girl child.
 
 
 
• **Low fertility rates**:
 
 
• Fertility transition often correlates with higher sex-ratio imbalances in societies with strong son preference, as families use sex-selection to ensure at least one male child within a smaller family size.

questions.question: Which act first allowed budget discussions in the Indian legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Councils Act, 1892**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Councils Act, 1892** was an act of the **British Parliament** that increased the number of additional members in the Central and Provincial legislative councils.
 
• For the first time in **British India**, the act empowered the legislative councils to discuss the **Annual Financial Statement**, commonly referred to as the **Budget**.
 
• Prior to this enactment, the legislative members had no legal right to participate in financial discussions or scrutinize the administrative expenditures of the **British Government**.
 
• It also introduced the provision for members to address questions to the **Executive** on matters of public interest, provided a mandatory six-day notice was given to the government.
 
• Despite these reforms, the act maintained significant limitations; members were strictly prohibited from asking **Supplementary Questions** or **Voting** on the budget.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1861**:

 
 
• It initiated the process of **Decentralization** by restoring legislative powers to the **Bombay** and **Madras Presidencies**.
 
• It introduced the **Portfolio System**, which gave legal recognition to the system introduced by **Lord Canning** in 1859.
 
• The **Viceroy** was empowered to issue **Ordinances** with a life span of six months during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)**:
 
 
• This act further expanded legislative functions, finally allowing members to ask **Supplementary Questions** and move resolutions on the **Budget**.
 
• It introduced **Communal Representation** for Muslims by accepting the concept of a **Separate Electorate**.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms)**:
 
 
• It introduced **Dyarchy** in the provinces, dividing subjects into **Reserved** and **Transferred** lists.
 
• It established a **Bicameral** legislature at the center consisting of an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).

questions.question: What is the one-time fee required to avail the FASTag Annual Pass seen in news in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 3000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)**, in collaboration with the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**, introduced the **FASTag Annual Pass** in **August 2025** to provide a cost-effective solution for frequent highway commuters.
 
• The one-time subscription fee for this pass is set at **Rs. 3000**, which allows private vehicle owners to enjoy unlimited or subsidized travel across a specified network of **National Highways** for a period of **365 days**.
 
• The primary objective of the **Rs. 3000** pass is to reduce the processing time at **Toll Plazas** and eliminate the need for frequent balance top-ups for daily travelers.
 
• This initiative leverages **Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)** technology, ensuring that the toll amount is validated through the centralized **National Electronic Toll Collection (NETC)** system without requiring the vehicle to stop.
 
• The fee structure was finalized after considering the average toll expenditure of a frequent traveler, aiming to promote a digital and cashless economy while optimizing traffic flow on major expressways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of FASTag:**

 
 
• The **FASTag** system was initially launched as a pilot project in **2014** on the Golden Quadrilateral.
 
• It was made mandatory for all M and N category vehicles from **February 15, 2021**, to ensure 100 percent electronic tolling.
 
• The **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)** acts as the central clearing house for all transactions.
 
 
 
• **Technological and Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The system uses **RFID tags** fixed on the vehicle’s windshield, which are scanned by sensors at toll booths.
 
• The implementation has led to a significant reduction in **Fuel Consumption** and **CO₂ emissions** by decreasing the idling time of vehicles at toll gates.
 
• Users receive real-time notifications via **SMS** and can manage their accounts through the **My FASTag App**.

questions.question: What is the audible range of sound for human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 Hz to 20000 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **audible range** for human beings is defined as the frequency interval of sound waves that can be detected by the healthy human ear, typically spanning from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Frequency** is the number of sound wave cycles per second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**; sounds within the human audible range stimulate the **auditory nerve** in the **inner ear**.
 
• The upper limit of human hearing, **20,000 Hz** (or **20 kHz**), is often the first frequency range to be affected by age or exposure to loud noises.
 
• Sound travels through air as a **longitudinal wave**, consisting of **compressions** and **rarefactions**, and its pitch is directly related to its frequency within this audible spectrum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasonic Sound**:

 
 
• These are sound waves with frequencies lower than **20 Hz**, which are below the threshold of human hearing.
 
• Large animals such as **elephants** and **whales** communicate over long distances using these low-frequency waves.
 
• Geological events like **earthquakes** and **volcanic eruptions** also generate infrasound.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasonic Sound**:
 
 
• Frequencies exceeding **20,000 Hz** are classified as ultrasonic or **ultrasound**.
 
• Animals such as **bats** and **dolphins** use ultrasound for **echolocation** to navigate and hunt prey in darkness or water.
 
• In technology, ultrasound is utilized in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) for measuring ocean depth and in medical **ultrasonography** for internal imaging.
 
 
 
• **Human Ear Sensitivity**:
 
 
• The human ear is most sensitive to frequencies between **2,000 Hz** and **5,000 Hz**, which is the range where most human speech resides.

questions.question: In Football, there are ____ types of free kicks awarded, depending on the nature of the offence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Law 13** of the **IFAB (International Football Association Board)** Laws of the Game, there are specifically two categories of free kicks awarded for fouls and misconduct: the **Direct Free Kick** and the **Indirect Free Kick**.
 
• A **Direct Free Kick** is awarded when a player commits a physical offence against an opponent in a manner considered by the referee to be careless, reckless, or using excessive force. Examples include **kicking**, **tripping**, **jumping at**, **striking**, or **pushing**. It is also awarded for **handball offences** (excluding the goalkeeper inside their own penalty area).
 
• A **Goal** can be scored directly from a **Direct Free Kick** against the opposing team without the ball touching any other player. If the kick is taken directly into the team’s own goal, a **Corner Kick** is awarded to the opposing team.
 
• An **Indirect Free Kick** is awarded for technical infractions or non-contact offences. Common reasons include **dangerous play**, **impeding the progress of an opponent** without contact, using **offensive language**, or specific **goalkeeper violations** like holding the ball for more than six seconds or handling a deliberate **back-pass** from a teammate.
 
• A **Goal** can only be scored from an **Indirect Free Kick** if the ball touches another player (from either team) before entering the net. If it goes into the goal without a second touch, a **Goal Kick** is awarded.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Referee Signals:**

 
 
• For an **Indirect Free Kick**, the **Referee** signals by raising their arm vertically above the head. This signal is maintained until the kick has been taken and the ball touches another player or goes out of play.
 
• For a **Direct Free Kick**, the referee points their arm in the direction of the attacking side to indicate the kick.
 
 
 
• **Required Distance:**
 
 
• In both types of free kicks, all opponents must be at least **9.15 meters** (or **10 yards**) away from the ball until it is in play, unless they are on their own goal line between the goalposts.
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Penalty Kicks:**
 
 
• If a player commits an offence that would normally result in a **Direct Free Kick** while inside their own **Penalty Area**, the referee awards a **Penalty Kick** instead of a free kick.

• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** is a baseline report developed and released by **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India). It serves as a rigorous tool to measure and monitor poverty across multiple dimensions simultaneously.

• These three dimensions are represented by **12 indicators**, including nutrition, child and adolescent mortality, maternal health, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, and bank accounts.
 
• The index contributes to tracking India's progress toward **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 1.2**, which aims to reduce at least by half the proportion of men, women, and children living in poverty in all its dimensions by **2030**.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 3 and 4?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **divisibility by 4** first: The last two digits must be divisible by 4.

Options 8123 and 8495 are **odd**, so they are not divisible by 4.

Option 9342: 42 is not divisible by 4. Option 8376: 76 ÷ 4 = 19 (Yes).

Check **divisibility by 3** for 8376: Sum of digits = 8 + 3 + 7 + 6 = 24. Since 24 is divisible by 3, 8376 is the answer.

**∴ The correct answer is 8376.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 8376, 8123, 8495, 9342.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Divisibility by 4:** Last two digits of the number must be divisible by 4.

2. **Divisibility by 3:** Sum of the digits of the number must be divisible by 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f126ce465d0d0b5b48f370ee97a904e8034f93aa59547d5940b744ae0bced32c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 8376: Last two digits = 76.

⇒ 76 ÷ 4 = 19 (Divisible by 4).

⇒ Sum of digits = 8 + 3 + 7 + 6 = 24.

⇒ 24 ÷ 3 = 8 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ For 9342: Last two digits = 42. 42 ÷ 4 = 10.5 (Not divisible by 4).

⇒ For 8123 and 8495: Both are odd numbers, so they cannot be divisible by 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 8376.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 12

A number is divisible by 12 if and only if it is divisible by both 3 and 4 simultaneously.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is an even number and the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 (divisible by both 2 and 3).

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the last three digits of the number are divisible by 8.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 3 and 11?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number divisible by both **3** and **11** must be divisible by **33**.

Check **3432**: Sum of digits = 3+4+3+2 = 12 (divisible by **3**).

Difference of alternate digits: (3+3) − (4+2) = 0 (divisible by **11**).

Checking other options shows none satisfy both criteria simultaneously.

**∴ The correct answer is 3432.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers are 3312, 3268, 3432, and 3520.

**Divisibility Rule of 3:** The **sum of all digits** of the number must be divisible by 3.

**Divisibility Rule of 11:** The **difference** between the sum of digits at **odd positions** and the sum of digits at **even positions** must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

⇒ **3312:** Sum = 3+3+1+2 = 9 (Divisible by 3). Difference = (3+1) − (3+2) = 4 − 5 = −1 (Not divisible by 11).

⇒ **3268:** Sum = 3+2+6+8 = 19 (Not divisible by 3).

⇒ **3432:** Sum = 3+4+3+2 = 12 (Divisible by 3). Difference = (3+3) − (4+2) = 6 − 6 = 0 (Divisible by 11).

⇒ **3520:** Sum = 3+5+2+0 = 10 (Not divisible by 3).

Since **3432** is the only number that satisfies both conditions, it is divisible by both 3 and 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 3432.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4 or are both zero.

Divisibility by 12

A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both its co-prime factors 3 and 4.

questions.question: Average of 6 consecutive odd natural numbers is 40. The just previous and the just next odd natural number to these 6 odd natural numbers are also included. What will be the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any set of **consecutive numbers** in an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the average is the **middle point** of the sequence.

The original average of 6 numbers is **40**.

When 1 number is added **just before** and 1 number **just after** the set, the **symmetry** of the sequence around the center remains unchanged.

Because the addition is **balanced** on both ends, the **mean** does not shift.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 6 consecutive odd natural numbers = 40.

**Formula:** Average of an AP = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1481eaaa2be4af57ad0b307a4cb6f88b406b848a81174413c8a43be67e6369f0.png] 

⇒ Let the 6 numbers be n₁, n₂, n₃, n₄, n₅, n₆.

⇒ Total Sum = Average × Count = 40 × 6 = 240.

⇒ The 6 consecutive odd numbers centered at 40 are: 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45.

⇒ **Just previous** odd number = 35 − 2 = 33.

⇒ **Just next** odd number = 45 + 2 = 47.

⇒ New total count = 8 numbers.

⇒ New Sum = 240 + 33 + 47 = 320.

⇒ New Average = 320 ÷ 8 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

The average of any sequence in AP is always exactly the middle term (if n is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if n is even).

Symmetry in Averages

Adding or removing terms symmetrically from both ends of an AP sequence never changes the average value.

Consecutive Odd/Even Numbers

The common difference (d) between any two consecutive odd or consecutive even numbers is always 2.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the number of **multiples** of a number **x** in the range **1 to n**, simply divide **n** by **x** and consider only the **integer quotient**.

Number of multiples = ⌊ 102 ÷ 5 ⌋

102 ÷ 5 = 20.4

The **integer quotient** is 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers range from **1 to 102**, Multiples of **5**.

**Formula Used:** n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1, where **l** is the last term, **a** is the first term, and **d** is the common difference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d43767687345b01872fdfc30cc73d3e466350bfe9e292758a9e3d398ed493b1.png] 

⇒ Multiples of 5 in the range are: 5, 10, 15, ..., 100.

⇒ This forms an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**.

⇒ First term (a) = 5

⇒ Last term (l) = 100

⇒ Common difference (d) = 5

⇒ n = [(100 − 5) ÷ 5] + 1

⇒ n = [95 ÷ 5] + 1

⇒ n = 19 + 1

⇒ n = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Number of Multiples in a Custom Range

To find multiples of **k** between **A** and **B**, the formula is ⌊ B ÷ k ⌋ − ⌊ (A − 1) ÷ k ⌋.

Divisibility Property

Every **nth** number in a sequence of integers is a multiple of **n**.

Sum of n Multiples

The sum of the first **n** multiples of **x** is given by the AP sum formula: Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × [First multiple + Last multiple].

Percentage Difference Formula

questions.question: A person spends 20 percent of his money. He deposits 70 percent of the remaining money in the bank. If Rs. 1680 are remaining with him now, then how much money he had initially?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining percentage of money = (100 − 20)% × (100 − 70)%

⇒ 80% × 30% = 24%

Given, 24% of **initial money** = Rs. 1680

⇒ 100% = (1680 ÷ 24) × 100 = 7000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Money spent = 20%

Deposit in bank = 70% of the **remaining money**

Final remaining amount = Rs. 1680

**Formula Used:**

Final Amount = Initial Amount × (1 − r₁/100) × (1 − r₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71afb0c4932aa61a64772ad1bdc5770f24269c50dd3f6a3c320e50486b73bb86.png] 

Let the **initial amount** be x.

⇒ Money left after 20% spending = x × (1 − 20/100) = 0.80x

⇒ Money left after 70% bank deposit = 0.80x × (1 − 70/100)

⇒ Final remaining = 0.80x × 0.30 = 0.24x

⇒ 0.24x = 1680

⇒ x = 1680 ÷ 0.24

⇒ x = 168000 ÷ 24

⇒ x = 7000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When values are changed sequentially, the final value is Initial × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100). For spending/depositing, use the minus sign.

Effective Percentage Method

The overall remaining percentage after successive reductions of a% and b% is (100 − a) × (100 − b) / 100 percent of the original value.

Fractional Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions (e.g., 20% = 1/5, 70% = 7/10) can often simplify complex multiplication in **ratio-based** problems.

questions.question: A alone can complete 60 percent part of a work in 18 days. A alone will complete 90 percent part of the same work in how many days?

Since the rate of work is constant, **Time** is directly proportional to the **Work Percentage**.

Ratio of work: 60% : 90% = 2 : 3

Therefore, the time ratio is also 2 : 3.

Given 2 units = **18 days**, then 1 unit = 9 days.

For **90% work** (3 units) = 3 × 9 = **27 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 days.**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A alone** for **60% work** = **18 days**.

**Formula Used:**

**Unitary Method**: Time for Required Work = (Given Time ÷ Given Work) × Required Work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f76931bb1e7c3ef698d569a78f6b9cac1a39acfa1a137d5dd93288824090578d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken to complete **60% work** = 18 days

⇒ Time taken = (3 ÷ 10) × 90 = 3 × 9

⇒ Time taken = **27 days**

questions.question: 3 men and 9 women together can complete a work in 18 days. A woman is twice as efficient as a man. How many men can complete this work in 14 days?

questions.question: Speed of A and B is 12 km/hr and 30 km/hr respectively. What will be the ratio of time taken by them to complete the same distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **Distance** is constant, the **Ratio of Time** taken is the inverse of the **Ratio of Speed**.

Speed Ratio (A : B) = 12 : 30 = 2 : 5

Time Ratio (A : B) = Inverse of Speed Ratio = 5 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of A (SA) = 12 km/hr

Speed of B (SB) = 30 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = Speed × Time

Time (T) = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0754775ad309430b998cade61a055beaf5d00e70eb117bd5322a4e9eab8906f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the constant distance be D km.

⇒ Time taken by A (TA) = D ÷ 12

⇒ Time taken by B (TB) = D ÷ 30

⇒ Ratio of time taken (TA : TB) = (D/12) : (D/30)

⇒ TA : TB = 30 : 12

⇒ Dividing both sides by 6, we get 5 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Speed and Time

For a constant distance, speed is **inversely proportional** to time. S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

When two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the **average speed** is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the **opposite direction**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. In the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.
